title: HCSO - Local law enforcement running Flock searches for FBI during Metro Surge

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: HCSO - Local law enforcement running Flock searches for FBI during Metro Surge
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting records about 11 Flock license plate reader searches the Hennepin County Sheriff's Office ran for FBI agents between January 14 and February 20, 2026, during Operation Metro Surge. The searches appear in a public Flock network audit with reasons such as "Obstructing Justice - FBI," "Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property - FBI Request," and "Threats/Harassment - fbi t gillman." They are listed below by date and Flock search ID.

1. The Sheriff's Office Flock Organization Audit entries for these 11 searches, as exported from Flock (CSV), including the name of the employee who ran each search, the full reason text, and the case number. Audit trail data are public under Minn. Stat. § 13.824, subd. 7(c).

2. For each search, the record of the factual basis and the associated case or complaint number that § 13.824, subd. 7(b) requires. 

3. The FBI's request for each search and the Sheriff's Office's response: the written request, form, or email from FBI staff (including the agents logged as T. Gillman, C. Olson, and Huver), and any record of what license plate reader data the Sheriff's Office sent back. January 1 to February 28, 2026.

4. Any policy, directive, or memo in effect between December 1, 2025 and February 28, 2026 on running license plate reader searches for federal agencies, including the FBI, ICE, HSI, or DHS.

5. Action logs, product logs, or similar internal tracking data used to document work done by the officers/analysts who ran the searches. If these contain sufficient detail, they are likely to satisfy item #2 as well.  

If any record is withheld as criminal investigative data, please identify it and cite the specific subdivision, as § 13.03, subd. 3(f) requires. Investigative data from an investigation that is no longer active are public under § 13.82, subd. 7.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Alan J. Segal
